name: Ikeshti Brood-Minder
body:
IKESHTI BROOD-MINDER
CR 2

XP 600
N Small humanoid (ikeshti, reptilian)
Init +5; Senses Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 12, flat-footed 14 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +1 natural, +2 armor)
hp 18 (4d8+0)
Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +4
Resist cold 5, fire 5

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 15 ft.
Melee 2 claws +4 (1d3+1 B&S)
Special Attacks squirt blood (1/day, DC 12 Fort, 30 ft.)

STATISTICS

Str 12 (+1), Dex 13 (+1), Con 11 (+0), Int 14 (+2), Wis 13 (+1), Cha 10 (+0)
Base Atk +3; CMB +3; CMD 14
Feats Improved Initiative, Iron Will
Skills Climb +9, Diplomacy +4, Heal +8, Perception +8; Survival +8 (+10 in deserts); Species Modifiers +2 Survival in deserts
Languages Common, Draconic

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Squirt Blood (Ex)

As a move action, a brood-minder can squirt blood from one of their eyes at a target within 30 feet. The target must attempt a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the brood-minder’s Hit Dice + the 20 brood-minder’s Constitution modifier) or become sickened for 1 round, plus an additional round for every 5 by which it fails the save. A brood-minder can use this ability once per day, plus one additional time per day for every 5 Hit Dice it has.

ECOLOGY

Environment any deserts, hills, or mountains
Organization solitary, team (2–4), or nest (5–12)
Treasure standard (leather armor)

Native to desert worlds, ikeshti are small reptilian humanoids with rust-colored scales. Various spines, fins, and horns grow along their heads, backs, and tails, helping to regulate their body temperature in the harsh desert climate. Hormonal changes in ikeshti can produce specialized variations of the species—including the following examples.

Specialized ikeshti who tend to the eggclutches and the young who emerge from them, brood minders are known for their detached, almost robotic personalities—and for obsessively defending their wards.

Meanwhile, many ikeshti exiled into the harsh desert go mad from the experience, transforming into near-mindless predators with razor-sharp claws and horns. These monsters continue to grow larger and more fearsome with each passing year, with those who survive long enough ultimately becoming ancient riveners.
